claim: Let \(n\ge 2\). For each \(r\in[1,\infty]\), let \(p_r=\|\cdot\|_r\) on \(\mathbb R^n\). Then \(p_r\) and \(p_s\) lie in the same intrinsic part of \(\mathcal N(\mathbb R^n)\) if and only if \(r=s\). For \(1<r<\infty\), the separating local triangular-defect asymptotic along \(e_1\) and \(e_1+t e_2\) is \(\Delta_{p_r}(e_1,e_1+t e_2)=((1-2^{1-r})/r)t^r+O(t^{2r})\). Consequently, for every \(n\ge 2\), the cone of equivalent norms on \(\mathbb R^n\) has continuum many intrinsic parts.
integrity: The proof separates theorem-level deductions from literature-search evidence. Search non-detection is not treated as a proof of novelty, and no numerical experiment is used as proof.
scientific_limitations: The result classifies only the canonical \(\ell^r\) norms on real \(\mathbb R^n\), not all intrinsic parts of the norm cone.

The finite-exponent separation is an elementary asymptotic consequence of the new triangular-defect criterion; an equivalent all-parameter corollary could exist under different terminology even though none was located.
No independent audit has been performed.
title: The finite-dimensional \(\ell^p\) scale yields continuum many intrinsic parts
